title: Per-pixel MODIS greenness trend, 2000 to 2025 (pixel_trend_long_record 1.0.0)
description:
Precomputed result of recipe pixel_trend_long_record 1.0.0 for Ait Bouguemez valley catchment: per-pixel 250 m Terra MOD13Q1 v6.1 growing-season NDVI Theil-Sen slopes and Mann-Kendall tests over 2000 to 2025 across 8094 catchment pixels. In the primary March to June window, the catchment median slope is +0.0076 NDVI per decade (spatial IQR +0.0037 to +0.0121); under Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate control (q = 0.05), 24.7% of catchment area lies in upward-FDR pixels, 0.1% in downward-FDR pixels, and 75.2% is not distinguished from zero. Per SCI-52, display rasters and the 16 geographic reveal frames show slope direction and magnitude only, never thresholded significance.

Each pixel's interval is one of thousands. With no change anywhere, about 2.5% of pixels would still show an upward and 2.5% a downward interval at the 95% level, so the shares are shown beside a false discovery rate check (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995, q = 0.05), the control Wilks (2016) recommends when many locations are tested at once, and the map shows the slope only, not which pixels pass. Neighbouring pixels are not independent: they share weather, snow and sensor effects. A connected area of pixels can arise from one shared cause, and the false discovery rate procedure was proved for independent tests. Each 250 m MODIS pixel mixes surfaces. Land cover shares use ESA WorldCover 2021, a single 2021 map, applied to every season. NDVI measures how green the ground looks from above, not forage, palatability or species: in Ait Bouguemez and the Central High Atlas, upper rangelands are dominated by spiny xerophytic vegetation over reduced short grasslands (SCI-19, p. 2), herders report the loss of palatable species (Astragalus armatus, Thymus satureioides) and the spread of unpalatable plants (Thymelaea virgata, Euphorbia nicaeensis) (SCI-03, pp. 7 to 8), and valley-floor apple orchards and irrigated fodder have expanded (SCI-03, pp. 5, 9 to 10; SCI-19, p. 9; SCI-105). The June to September window spans the transition from late-spring pastoral agdal closure into open summer high-pasture grazing before transhumant flocks leave the valley in September and October (SCI-03, pp. 5 to 6, 12; SCI-19, pp. 2 to 5, Table 1; SCI-96); exact opening dates vary by village assembly and year. These trends are not adjusted for rainfall; restrend_long_record states how closely the place's greenness follows antecedent rain. Trend methods can miss real change: in simulations for southern Africa, 30 to 40% degradation was needed before a trend showed under a rainfall-driven increase (Wessels et al. 2012). An interval that includes zero is not evidence of no change. In the spring windows, upper slopes are snow-covered for part of the window. Composites keep only pixels flagged good or marginal, but earlier or later snowmelt can change spring greenness with no change in the plants. Terra's overpass has drifted earlier since 2020, from 10:30 to about 9:06 mean local time by December 2025 (NASA): later seasons are seen with a lower sun and longer shadows in mountain terrain, which may shift NDVI without any change on the ground.

providers.processing:lineage: Anonymous SAS-signed range reads of MOD13Q1 v6.1 NDVI and pixel reliability windows over the frozen geometry from Planetary Computer (584 Terra composites); per-pixel growing-season means, Theil-Sen slopes, Mann-Kendall tests and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across 8094 catchment pixels; EPSG:3857 slope-only display overviews and 16 outlet-ordered reveal frames (science/pipeline/pixel_trend_long_record.py). Web-ready derived assets (pixel-trend-mar_jun-cells.json) are copies of the canonical GeoTIFF values written by science/pipeline/web-assets.py.

siterra:dataset.access_route: https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1 collection modis-13Q1-061, assets 250m_16_days_NDVI and 250m_16_days_pixel_reliability, anonymous SAS-signed COG range reads
siterra:dataset.resolution_note: Native 250 m MODIS sinusoidal grid (231.66 m cells), 16-day composites; display overviews on a 30 m EPSG:3857 grid

siterra:geo_selection.area_method: Count of 10 m analysis pixels whose centres fall inside the frozen polygon, EPSG:32629

operation_order: NDVI(p, c) = DN / 10000 for Terra MOD13Q1 v6.1 composite c and 250 m pixel p, kept only where the composite's pixel reliability is 0 (good) or 1 (marginal) and -0.2 <= NDVI <= 1.0, as in restrend_long_record

G(p, y, W) = mean of the kept NDVI(p, c) over the 16-day periods starting in a month of growing window W in year y, defined only when at least half of those periods (rounded up) are kept at p; a period with no Terra product on the archive read counts as nothing kept
Pixels: every MOD13Q1 pixel holding at least one 10 m analysis cell of the catchment; w(p) = number of those cells

Per pixel and window: over the season years where G is defined, the Theil-Sen slope of G on the year (median of pairwise slopes) with Sen's 95% interval from the ranks (N - C) / 2 and (N + C) / 2 + 1 of the N sorted pairwise slopes, C = 1.96 sqrt(n (n - 1) (2n + 5) / 18), no tie correction, as in restrend_long_record; fewer than 15 seasons and the pixel is insufficient_seasons

Per pixel: the Mann-Kendall statistic S with the tie-corrected variance n (n - 1) (2n + 5) / 18 minus the sum over tie groups of t (t - 1) (2t + 5) / 18, Z = (S - sign(S)) / sqrt(variance), two-sided p from the standard normal distribution
Pixel direction: Sen's interval entirely above zero is upward, entirely below zero downward, otherwise includes_zero

False discovery rate check: Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.05 over every pixel with a slope in the window; a pixel whose p passes keeps its direction as upward_fdr or downward_fdr when its Sen interval agrees, otherwise not_distinguished

Area groups: the catchment; each class of each strata layer listed in the configuration; the fixed elevation bands named in the configuration; the land cover groups of the configuration (WorldCover 2021 classes). For each group, the share of its 10 m analysis cells that lie in upward, downward, includes_zero and insufficient_seasons pixels, and the same for the false discovery rate classes. Under no change anywhere, about 2.5% of pixels per direction would show a per-pixel interval by chance; this is stated beside the shares

Connected areas: 8-connected groups of pixels sharing a false discovery rate direction (primary) or a per-pixel interval direction (sensitivity), of at least minClusterPixels pixels (Ait Bouguemez: 4, about 21 ha). For each: pixel count, catchment area in km2, centroid (longitude, latitude) weighted by catchment cells, median elevation of its catchment cells, land cover and aspect shares, median slope and its range. Every downward area is listed; upward areas are counted with the five largest listed

Display: for each window, the Theil-Sen slope in NDVI per decade averaged into the fixed EPSG:3857 grid of the map overviews (pixelM metres), painted with the light-theme data.ndvi-departure arms on the fixed domain of the configuration (Ait Bouguemez: -0.05 to +0.05 per decade, unpainted within 0.0025 of zero, t = (|d| - neutral) / (domain - neutral) clamped to 0..1, opacity 0.10 + 0.70 t, t in steps). No direction or false discovery rate class is drawn on the display

Data rasters: for each window, a GeoTIFF on the native MOD13Q1 grid with the slope, lower and upper bound per decade, and the number of seasons; no pixel-wise p-value or false discovery rate class is stored as a map raster (SCI-52)

siterra:checks.name: recompute_sample_period
siterra:checks.detail: 26 evenly spaced catchment pixels in mar_jun recomputed independently from the stored MOD13Q1 windows: largest Theil-Sen slope difference 0.0000089 NDVI per decade (tolerance 1e-5). All 16 reveal-step PNG frames verified against catchment outlet distance ordering.

siterra:checks.name: nodata_not_zero
siterra:checks.detail: NDVI fill (-3000) and values outside -0.2 to 1.0 are not observed; pixel reliability other than [0, 1], including fill 255, is not observed; pixels with fewer than 15 seasons are insufficient_seasons and transparent on display rasters, never painted as zero.

siterra:checks.name: units_and_scale
siterra:checks.detail: Every stored NDVI window is int16 with nodata -3000 and GDAL scale 10000 (physical value = DN / 10000). Pixel reliability windows are uint8 with nodata 255, except 4 stored as int8 with nodata -1. Slopes and interval bounds are reported in NDVI per decade (1/(10 a)).

siterra:checks.name: qa_join_coverage
siterra:checks.detail: All 584 composites share one 176 x 131 pixel window grid; 8094 MOD13Q1 pixels hold the 4173603 analysis cells of the catchment. In the registered growing windows: 7 composite periods absent from Planetary Computer (A2024225, A2025193, A2025209, A2025225, A2025241, A2025257, A2025273); on 2026-10-28 NASA CMR listed 7 of them (held by the NASA archive, which needs an Earthdata login, not used).

siterra:checks.name: period_alignment
siterra:checks.detail: A composite belongs to a season when its 16-day period starts in a month of the growing window of that year.

siterra:checks.name: attribution_present
siterra:checks.detail: MOD13Q1 v6.1 citation with DOI, subset and access date, ESA WorldCover 2021 attribution and Copernicus DEM notices are in siterra:attribution.
